tossups.text: A poetry collection by John Wilson influenced a play by this author in which a priest attempts to stop the Chairman from leading a group of revelers in singing ditties while their city goes to hell. A character created by this author asks "why did you come to visit us / In this forgotten quiet place?" in a letter in which she "write[s] to you...when that is said / What more is left for me to say?" In another play, this author created a character who is increasingly upset that God rewarded his lazier rival and pours poison in the rival's drink, confirming that "villainy and genius / are two things that can never go together." This writer's plays Feastin the Time of Plague and Mozart and Salieri are two of four "little tragedies." This writer used iambic tetrameter with alternating masculine and feminine rhymes in the stanzas of his magnum opus, in which the title character duels Lensky and rejects Tatyana. For 10 points, name this Russian author of Eugene Onegin.

A character with this last name remembers giving his brother wildflowers and wins a fistfight by tripping his nephew. A woman with this last name admits her husband was "never in the paper," but declares "attention must be paid." A man with this last name imitates his math teacher's lisp and deems his father "a phony little fake" after he gives his mistress somestockings.Flute music accompanies the reveries of a character with this last name, who insists that his neighbor Charley is not "well liked" and fatally crashes his car for the life insurance money. For 10 points, identify this surname of Linda, Biff, and Willy from Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman.

this structure is essential for vaccines and immunization. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this vaccine-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The vaccine is a key component of the Immune system, involved in vaccines and immunization.

tossups.text: In human anatomy, this structure is essential for white blood cell types. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this erythrocyte-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The erythrocyte is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in white blood cell types.

tossups.text: After this dynasty captured King Francis I [the first] at the Battle of Pavia, Francis traded Burgundy for his freedom, then almost immediately resumed fighting against this dynasty. Inbreeding may have caused members of this dynasty to develop a pronounced lower jaw. The 1713 Pragmatic Sanction was a failed attempt to give this dynasty's possessions to a female heir, Maria Theresa. For nearly four continuous centuries, the Holy Roman Emperor was a member of, for 10 points, what dynasty that ruled Austria?

One artist's set design for this ballet contains fencing that may have been inspired by the art from Japanese internment camps. An hour-glass shaped rocking chair sits under diagonal lines outlining a roof in the original set of this ballet scored for a thirteen-instrument chamber orchestra. Hart Crane's poem "The Bridge" is the source for the title of this ballet with set design by Isamu Noguchi. The daily life of the Wife and Husbandsman are depicted in this ballet through five variations on the Shaker hymn "Simple Gifts." For 10 points, name this ballet choreographed by Martha Graham and with music by Aaron Copland.

This scientist discovered a law that states that different genes in an organism do not affect each other when creating new reproductive cells. This scientist is famous for his observations on pea plants while studying at a monastery. For 10 points, name this scientist, often called the "Father of Genetics."

The consequences of humans receiving substances differing in this trait include agglutination or a deadly "incompatibility reaction." A portion of this trait is determined by the presence of Rhesus factor, or Rh. About seven percent of humans carry a form of this trait that makes them "universal donors." When performing a transfusion, this trait must usually match for the donor and recipient. For 10 points, name this trait for humans that can be A, B, O, or AB, depending on the chemicals on red blood cells.

These comprise the "pair" devices named for Sziklai and Darlington. Their operation is described by the Ebers-Moll model; they can operate in cutoff, saturation, inverse, or active modes depending on the emitter, base, and collector voltages. The first of these devices was the point-contact one built in 1947 by Bardeen, Brattain, and Shockley; junction ones were later employed in IC's. For 10 points, name these electronic devices that have largely replaced vacuum tubes and underpin almost all modern electronics.

A quantity describing this force is plotted against the Hersey number on the Stribeck curve. Observations with atomic force microscopes verified Amonton's first law of this force. This force, which is studied in tribology ["tribe-ology"], can be caused by asperities ["uh-SPARE-uh-teez"]. It's not related to electricity, but Coulomb's model for the "dry" type of this force states that it equals the normal force times mu. The coefficient of the "static" type of this force is very low for materials such as Teflon and ice. For 10 points, name this force between two contacting surfaces that resists motion.

It was at a speech in this state that Senator Joe McCarthy claimed he had a list of 57 State Department employees who were communists. John Sayles' 1987 film Matewan depicts a shootout between union members and the Baldwin-Felts Detective Agency in this state in 1920. One participant in that shootout was Sheriff Sid Hatfield, a relative of the family from this state involved in the feud with the McCoys. This state was created after seceding from an already-seceded state during a vote at the Second Wheeling Convention. For 10 points what US state is home to Harper's Ferry, where John Brown took the federal arsenal, and which has capital at Charleston?

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for intestinal enzymes. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this duodenum-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The duodenum is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in intestinal enzymes.

tossups.text: A week after its 1924 "saber-noise," Luis Altamirano led a military coup in this country against Arturo Alessandri Palma. In this country, Victor Jara and other protestors were executed in a stadium he now names. The assassination of Orlando Letelier was accomplished in Washington DC, with US aid, by this country's DINA secret police as part of Operation Condor. A 1973 coup in this country's La Moneda palace began a right-wing military junta whose economic advisors, the "Chicago Boys," championed free-market capitalism. For 10 points, name this country in South America where Salvador Allende was replaced by Augusto Pinochet in Santiago.

The Hadith of Jabir notes that the first things created with light by Allah were the pen, the tablet, water, and this kind of object. The Zoroastrian Nowruz holiday celebrates a notable event involving a jewel-encrusted example of this object belonging to Jamshid. The prophet Zechariah has a vision of the sinful priest Joshua standing next to one of these objects. Muhammad recommended nightly recitations of a prayer named for this kind of object, which in Revelation is flanked by a man, an ox, an eagle, and a lion - all of whom are winged and covered in eyes. A passage named for this kind of object concludes that Allah is the highest and most glorious, and is the 255th aya in the Cow Surah. For 10 points, name this celestial object upon which God rests in both Christianity and Islam.

The Tower commission was appointed to investigate what had occurred during this event. One of the actions that occurred during this event had earlier been outlawed by the Boland amendment. One of the main participants in this event now runs a show called War Stories on Fox News. One of the results of this event was the consensus that the president seemed not to have a frim grasp on what was going on in his administration, especially in the defense department headed by Caspar Weinberger, which may be why he was nicknamed the "Teflon" president. George H. W. Bush pardoned many officials involved in, FTP, what affair which saw the U. S. trade arms to for Iranian hostages and then use the proceeds from those sells to support a namesake insurgency group in Nicaragua?

This function is used the Fourier transform of an [emphasize]even function, and a law named for this function provides a generalized form of the Pythagorean theorem. This function is given by the x-coordinate on the unit circle, and the reciprocal of this function is secant. In right-triangle trigonometry, this function of an angle is found by dividing the adjacent leg by the hypotenuse. For 10 points, name this trig function that sine is divided by to produce tangent.

Several religious summer camps in this province are located around the shore of its Skeleton Lake. Over two-thirds of this province's population is located in an area called the Golden Horseshoe. Territory in this province provides the western shore for the James Bay, and the Rainy River forms part of the southeastern border of this province. The long-running Niagara Escarpment overlooks this province's city of Hamilton. One city in this province is home to the tallest building in the country; that building is the CN Tower. For 10 points, name this province that gives its name to a Great Lake, and also contains the capital of Canada, Ottawa.

Small dust particles comprise this body's toroidal "halo" ring and its very faint "gossamer" ring. The Oval BA is a large storm within the atmosphere of this planet. In July 1994, scars were visible in this object's atmosphere due to its collision with the comet Shoemaker-Levy 9. Moons of this planet include the reddest object of the Solar System called Amalthea, as well as one another whose tidal interactions with it cause it to be the most volcanic object in the solar system. This planet's most notable feature is a persisting cloudy anti-cyclonic storm in its southern hemisphere. For 10 points, name this fifth planet from the sun, which contains the Great Red Spot.

The protagonist of this short story has a fishing rod called Killall, which scares trout enough to want to jump in his pockets. Another man in this story hits rock bottom when his plowshare crashes on a rock and his horse starts coughing. In this story, Miser Stevens' voice is heard coming out of a handkerchief. A resident of Marshfield partially titles this story, which references a Whittier poem when one character predicts another's future, saying "They will call you Ichabod." In this story, Judge Hathorne presides over a jury of twelve dead men, who rule in favor of Jabez Stone against Scratch. For 10 points, name this story in which a New Hampshire farmer's soul is saved by the lawyering of an American senator, by Stephen Vincent Benet.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for tonsils and malt. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this lymph-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The lymph is a key component of the Immune system, involved in tonsils and malt.

parts.text: Identify this literary family that also includes Blanca, who falls in love with Pedro Tercero Garcia; Clara, who predicts an earthquake that destroys Tres Marias; and the patriarch Esteban.
This Chilean author created the Trueba family for her novel House of the Spirits. She also wrote Daughter of Fortune and Eva Luna.
This most recent Allende novel sees a slave named Zarité from Saint-Domingue relocate to New Orleans, where she is aided by Violette the prostitute and the witch Tante Rose.

bonuses.leadin: Upon marrying into this family, one member is horrified by a gift of a rug made out of her dog Barrabas. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this title of a poem that opens, "virtuous men pass mildly away, / And whisper to their souls to go." The speaker of that poem with this title says, "If they be two, they are two so / As stiff twin compasses are two."
"A Valediction: Forbidding Mourning" is by this Metaphysical poet, who included "Death be not proud" in his collection Holy Sonnets.

Donne's "The Canonization" opens, "For God's sake hold your tongue, and let me [do this action]." The speaker of an Elizabeth Barrett Browning poem says to "Let me count the ways" she does this action.

bonuses.leadin: The speaker of an Adrienne Rich poem with this title says, "when I think of a landscape I am thinking of a time. / When I talk of taking a trip I mean forever" and "The grammar turned and attacked me." For 10 points each:

What is the main function of the colon in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to gut microbiome.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with red blood cells and hemoglobin.
What is the main function of the erythrocyte in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to red blood cells and hemoglobin.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name this 1956 conflict in which Israel invaded Egypt in response to Gamal Abdel Nasser's nationalization of the namesake canal near the Sinai Peninsula.
This first Israeli Prime Minister signed the Protocol of Sèvres.

Canadian Prime Minister Lester Pearson's efforts to actually mediate the Suez Crisis earned him this annual diplomatic prize. This prize is awarded in Oslo, while similar prizes for Literature, Chemistry, Physics, and Medicine are awarded in Stockholm.

bonuses.leadin: The secret Protocol of Sèvres was a plan for Great Britain and France to "mediate" this event, in which they would take over the waterway in question. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this composer of the Russian Easter Festival Overture, whose opera The Tale of Tsar Saltan contains "The Flight of the Bumblebee".
A muted trumpet and trombone play a fanfare in "The Kalendar Prince," the second movement of this Rimsky-Korsakov suite. Other movements include "The Sea and Sinbad's Ship." A
This student and friend of Rimsky-Korsakov wrote the ballet The Seasons, a Slavonian Symphony, the symphonic poem Stenka Razin, and a concerto for alto saxophone.

bonuses.leadin: He re-orchestrated Mussorgsky's A Night on Bald Mountain and featured a solo violin in his orchestral Capriccio Espagnol. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these large spheres of plasma and gas.
These stars, whose lower temperatures produce their namesake color, lie on the upper right side of the HR diagram. These stars will eventually become white dwarves.
This stage is the beginning and longest stage of a star's life. Hydrogen fuses into helium as the star expands in it.

bonuses.leadin: These entities are classified by luminosity and temperature in the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram. For 10 points:

parts.text: The intersection of two lines creates four angles; no matter what angles are created, what is the sum of the degree measurements of those four angles?
Of those four angles, there will be two pairs of angles with equal measurement that are on opposite sides of the intersection point. This term describes those equal angles.

This term describes a line that intersects two other lines at two different points; if those two other lines are parallel, this line creates pairs of equal alternating angles and equal corresponding angles.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, give the following about intersecting lines.

parts.text: Name this phenomenon in which namesake gases cause thermal radiation to be re-emitted in all directions. It is named for a structure used to control the climate of plants.
This is the most abundant greenhouse gas in Earth's atmosphere, although both methane and carbon dioxide are stronger contributors to the greenhouse effect.

To calculate the effects of the greenhouse effect, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change proposed this quantity, which is defined as the difference between outgoing and incoming radiation at the tropopause.

bonuses.leadin: A "runaway" form of this effect on the planet Venus is an example of a positive feedback loop in the atmospheric sciences. For 10 points each:

parts.text: These species are represented as a "y" in the Lotka-Volterra equations. These animals include lynxes and foxes, which hunt for animals like hares.

The Lotka-Volterra equations do not have a term for this property of a population. The differential equation for logistical growth multiplies k P by one minus population over this property. Organisms with high growth rates can overshoot this limit.

The paradox of these creatures, due to their high diversity, is unresolved by the Lotka-Volterra equations. One class of these creatures is heterotrophic and they include organisms like dinoflagellates.

bonuses.leadin: Population cycles of species can be predicted using the Lotka-Volterra equations, which are a set of differential equations. For 10 points each, answer some questions about the Lotka-Volterra model:

parts.text: Name this political ideology which takes its name from a bundle of sticks used in Rome and rejects individuality in favor of nationalism.

Fascism was influenced by this nineteenth-century ideology which broadly applied the title thinker's "survival of the fittest" to justify capitalism's lack of regard for the poorest. Its advocates included Herbert Spencer.

Fascism rejects a modern theory named after this kind of "peace," which explicates Monadic and Dyadic forms of the title phenomenon. In that theory, the namesake governments don't go to war with each other.

bonuses.leadin: The best example of this ideology in Latin America is the Integralism developed by Brazil's Plinio Salgado. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with bone structure and types.
What is the main function of the skull in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to bone structure and types.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: Name this weapon, other examples of which included the Panther and the Tiger models of Nazi Germany. The Molotov cocktail was originally designed to counter these weapons during the Winter War.
The KV and T-34 were some of the tanks used by this country as it fought Nazi Germany on the Eastern Front of World War II. This country was led by Joseph Stalin for the duration of the war.

This 1943 battle on the Eastern Front was the largest tank battle in history. This battle was codenamed Operation Citadel and included nearly one thousand German and Soviet tanks fighting at Prokhorovka.

bonuses.leadin: The Battle of Raseiniai saw the use of the KV model of this weapon. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this diagram that typically consists of 11 nodes, with Kether at the top and Malkuth at the bottom, plus 22 connecting lines.
The Tree of Life illustrates the cosmology of this religious tradition frequently described as "Jewish mysticism."

Many of the concepts depicted in the Tree of Life appear in this first century CE text attributed to Nehunya ben HaKanah. This is the earliest known text that links the numerical meaning of the sefirot to aspects of God.

bonuses.leadin: Due to disagreements over the correct number of paths to show on this diagram, contemporary traditions sometimes distinguish between versions of "Emanation" and versions of "Return". For 10 points each:

parts.text: This hero of the Rif Wars and Generalísimo of the army won the Spanish Civil War. Succeeded by Juan Carlos, he ruled as dictator from 1939 until his death in 1975.
Franco became the leader of this fascist party in Spain after it merged with the Carlists. Its name is Spanish for a certain Roman military formation.
A father named Miguel with this surname ruled Spain as a dictator from 1923-30. His son José Antonio founded the Falange, and was killed by the Spanish Republicans.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer some questions about the Spanish Civil War.

parts.text: Name this reproductive part of a plant that has petals.
This is the "male" organ of the flower. It consists of a pollen-producing anther on top of a filament.
These seed-bearing plants are distinguished from gymnosperms by the fact that they produce flowers.

bonuses.leadin: These structures often produce nectar to attract pollinators, such as hummingbirds and bees. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this large region in Russia east of the Ural Mountains, whose namesake semi-permanent anticyclone is responsible for its extremely cold and dry winters. It is spanned by a railway running from Moscow to Vladivostok.

Siberia also contains a large example of these geologic features, which are formed by rapid accumulation of mafic rock. The volcanic fissure eruptions that created one of these features in the Deccan Plateau may have contributed to the K-Pg mass extinction.

parts.text: The divergent boundary between the Amurian and Eurasian Plates in southeastern Siberia created this deep rift lake. The Angara River drains this largest freshwater lake by volume.

bonuses.leadin: This region's vast, swampy western plain contains some of the largest peatlands in the world. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this task, for which the best known algorithms are Quickthis and Mergethis, and the very slow Bubblethis. It is the task of putting elements of a list in particular order.

Selection sort is sometimes described as an example of this algorithm design paradigm in which the locally optimal choice is selected at each step. Dijkstra's algorithm is another example of class of algorithms for shortest path.

Another greedy algorithm is this encoding scheme named for this man which generates his namesake trees based on the frequency of characters and then encodes the most common characters with the shortest strings.

bonuses.leadin: Algorithms for this common task include one developed by Tony Hoare which randomly selects a pivot against which to make comparisons. For 10 points:

parts.text: The first writing James Joyce did that became part of Finnegans Wake was this short sketch, in which the titular monarch of Ireland cleans up after a party by drinking the dregs from his guests' glasses.

Joyce described "Roderick O'Conor" as his first writing "since the final Yes of Ulysses," referring to the novel's concluding monologue by Molly, a woman with this surname. Her husband, Leopold, is the novel's protagonist.
A few months after "Roderick O'Conor," Joyce wrote a sketch with the title "Here Comes Everybody," which he uses as the nickname of this main character of Finnegans Wake.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about the creation of Finnegans Wake, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with phagocytes and macrophages.
What is the main function of the phagocyte in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to phagocytes and macrophages.
